### ① Derived judgments

- Lines 31–33 (rule 1) require of an L1 reviewer: REWORK any PR that commits a one-off codegen, codemod or migration script whose output is the PR's own diff; run that script personally from the PR branch history or an attachment; find its proof readings (byte-identity, exports-equality) in the PR body. Tools that run again after merge (gates, regen steps, customer codemods from a migration guide) are excluded. RIGHT against the card's item 1 and its out-of-scope bullet, clause for clause; the card's FAIL is rendered as REWORK, the L1 verdict word.
- Lines 31–33 require of a dev: keep the script out of the merged tree, leave it in branch history or attach it, and write the proof readings into the PR body. RIGHT against the card, and in line with the existing os-dev.md rule that one-off proofs are quoted in the PR body and leave no permanent file.
- Line 34 (rule 2) requires of an L1 reviewer: for a move or split whose net growth is far beyond a pure move, account per file for what each extra block is for, record it in the ACCEPT comment, and REWORK if it cannot be accounted. RIGHT against the card's item 2 ("the account goes in the review record"; the L1 review record is the ACCEPT comment per execution-duties.md 〈L1 审核〉).
- Card item 3 (rule recorded on #33949) is met outside the diff by comment 6911407209.
- Target file: the card names `references/review-checklist.md`, which on main is a one-line pointer stub to `l1-review-checklist.md`; writing into the stub's target is RIGHT. No pointer line was added to SKILL.md or contract-review.md; none is needed, as execution-duties.md already routes every L1 reviewer to this file.

### ② Semver level

- No published package is touched: `.claude/**` and `scripts/pm/**` ship nothing. `skip-changeset` is the correct route under the checklist's own line 20 (no empty changeset); `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.
- `Clause-②: no` is correct: no served behaviour becomes refused; the diff is rule text and one ceiling number.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct: no metadata key, schema or protocol surface is touched.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation, edited `l1-review-checklist.md` instead of the claim's literal path: answered, correct (rename on main, stub points there).
- Deviation, edited `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` outside the claim surface: answered, required. The file sat at headroom 0, and the ratchet rule itself orders the CEILINGS row moved in the same PR.
- Deviation, PR body asked for maintainer approval as if Tier H: answered. The body now reads Tier S with nothing asked of the maintainer (final-head comment 6913225508); the head did not move.
- Deviation, the area's common rule listing `.claude/**` as out of bounds: answered by the card, which sends the work there on the maintainer's order and records it as an explicit exception to the wind-down.
- `open_questions`: empty. `security_findings`: none; confirmed, no hunk teaches permission, credential or auth behaviour.
- `check:pm-dispatch-gates` reported NOT MEASURED locally: answered by this head's check-run `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, conclusion success.
- Out-of-scope note, the dispatch-gates self-test case that reds when the tracked-file set changes mid-run: noted by the dev with no carrier. ESCALATED to the seat to file or dismiss; it is not this PR's defect.
- Check-runs on this head: 28 success, 25 skipped, none failed, including `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and both `PR-body guards` runs.
- SQL push-down: n/a, no query in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

`l1-review-checklist.md` against the card's ruling and the rules beside it on main:

- Agreement: nothing in lines 31–34 contradicts SKILL.md 〈优先级〉 or 〈审核两级〉, any ⛔ line there, execution-duties.md 〈L1 审核〉, os-dev.md or AGENTS.md. The lines sit in the L1 file only, so the L2 read-only shape is untouched (L1 rules do not reach L2). The existing REWORK line for over-budget expansion in execution-duties.md is adjacent to rule 2, not restated by it.
- New gate: none. These are L1 review criteria the maintainer named in the ruling the card quotes; no script, check or CI gate is added.
- Restatement: none. No other file on main carries either rule.
- Id-lint: the four lines carry no issue number; the ids live in the ratchet script's comment, the convention for that map.
- S1 (should-fix) — line 31 reads 「⛔ 不入仓,提交即判 REWORK」 while line 32 says the script 「住 PR 分支历史」. A script is in branch history only by having been committed to the branch, so a literal reader can REWORK a PR that followed line 32 exactly (script in an earlier commit, absent at head). The card carries the same looseness; the intent is plainly the merged tree. An in-place rewording of the trigger, for example 「head 的 diff 含它即判 REWORK」, costs no line. Non-blocking: the two lines read together resolve it.
- N1 (nit) — 「净增远超纯移动」 has no threshold; it mirrors the card's "far beyond" and is left to the reviewer's judgment.
- N2 (nit) — record 6911407209 puts the per-file breakdown in the dev's PR body with the reviewer checking it; the checklist, following the card, puts the account on the reviewer. The card governs. os-dev.md carries no dev-side line, so a dev first meets rule 1 at REWORK; the card scoped the change to the checklist, so this is a follow-up for the seat to weigh, not a defect here.

`scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` against the ratchet's own rule (script header, and the guard row in SKILL.md):

- Ruling quoted in the PR body: yes. The body names the card #34343 body as ruling of record with the maintainer's words verbatim, and links ruling record 6911407209. Card-body-as-ruling follows the landed rows for #29160 and #29420. The ruling orders both rules into the review checklist, which is what the rule asks of a raise.
- Measured delta quoted: yes, 76 → 80, +4. Verified on the tree: main's file is 76 lines, the head's is 80.
- Ceiling moved by at most the delta: yes, 76 → 80, headroom 0, landed count.
- Re-wrap: none. The checklist diff is four pure additions, no existing line touched; the added lines are 109, 113, 111 and 120 bytes, each one rule clause the card ordered, none padded or split to buy a line.
- No other CEILINGS row moves in this PR; `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` concluded success on this head.
